executiveSummary.summary: The reviewed Salesforce evidence indicates a generally supportable platform with several material areas requiring remediation. The most significant themes relate to automation efficiency, access governance and maintainability. Findings in this sample are illustrative only.
keyThemes: Several maintainability improvements can reduce future delivery risk.
recommendedNextActions: Confirm unresolved context with the platform owner.
Sequence Medium findings into the remediation backlog.

coverage.summary: No critical issue was identified in the reviewed evidence.

findings.title: Broad execution criteria on invoice automation
findings.observation: The record-triggered flow executes after create or update without entry criteria in the reviewed metadata.

evidence.detail: The start element is configured for create/update and no restrictive entry criteria were identified.

guidance.summary: Current Salesforce automation guidance recommends designing record-triggered automation with intentional entry conditions and transaction behaviour appropriate to the use case.

findings.gap: The flow evaluates every qualifying save rather than narrowing execution to the business-state transition that drives invoice creation.
findings.risk: At higher transaction volume this can add unnecessary automation work and increase transaction complexity.
findings.recommendation: Review the intended business trigger and narrow start conditions where supported by the current process and Salesforce guidance.

positiveFindings.title: Fault handling is present
positiveFindings.summary: The reviewed flow includes a defined fault-handling path, providing an explicit mechanism for surfaced failures.

componentHighlights.reason: Selected because it supports a material automation finding.

limitations: This example is metadata-oriented and does not include production runtime telemetry.
Data quality was not independently sampled.
